newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end choppy session little changed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end choppy session little changed.

text.p: Wall Street stocks finished mixed on Tuesday, with blue chips eking out slim gains in a choppy session that analysts said highlighted the market's concern and uncertainty about interest rates.

"The market is very divided on the outlook for interest rate policy," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates. "Right now there's no compelling evidence to drive us in either direction."
The Dow industrials rose six points to 7085. Broader indices finished slightly lower.
U.S. Treasuries were weaker on the day, pushing the yield on the benchmark 30-year bond up to 6.85 percent from 6.81 percent on Monday.
Analysts said the market's tone was likely to become even more cautious as the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on March 25 approached.
"Basically, this market has been put on wait," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons. "We're going to have more of this ragged action until we get past the FOMC meeting."
Within the relatively mixed picture of the overall market, there were some subtle shifts at play, analysts noted, with investors taking profits in strong sectors and buying up some recent laggards.
"Some of the groups that have had outstanding performances appeared to be catching their breath," White said, citing banking and pharmaceutical issues in particular.
Among drug stocks, Amgen Inc dipped 1-1/2 to 61-1/4 and Eli Lilly and Co shed 2-3/4 to 88-3/4.
Chase Manhattan Corp slipped 3-1/8 to 106-1/2 and BankAmerica Corp fell 3-3/8 to 119-5/8.

Steel companies finished broadly higher, led by USX-U.S. Steel Corp, which gained 1-3/8 to 30-1/8 and Inland Steel Industries Inc up one point to 20-1/8, after an industry report showed shipments from U.S. steel mills rose by 7.3 percent in January versus December.
The increase was 5.5 percent when compared to a year ago, according the report by the American Iron and Steel Institute.

Stocks, particularly blue chips, got a vote of confidence from Fidelity Investments' Magellan Fund, which said today it increased the share of its portfolio invested in stocks to 93.5 percent at January 31 from 89.6 percent a month earlier.

Fidelity said Intel Corp, General Electric Co and Philip Morris Cos Inc remained Magellan's top three holdings after the period, but that General Motors Corp was replaced by Citicorp among the fund's top 10 holdings.
But despite the massive fund's increased appetite for stocks, analysts said the market remained hostage to its more immediate concerns, those over interest rates.
In individual issues, Tessco Technologies Inc tumbled 12-3/8 to 20-1/8 after the company warned its fourth quarter earnings would be below analysts' estimates.

Wyle Electronics slid five points to 33-3/8 after that company also warned about upcoming earnings. Wyle said it expected its first quarter earnings would be below those in the previous quarter as well as those of a year ago.

Nike Inc fell 5/8 to 66-3/8, rebounding off a session low of 63. The shares were hit early in the day by a rumor that Woolworth Corp's Foot Locker unit had reduced orders for Nike athletic shoes, a rumor Woolworth later denied. Shares in Woolworth gained 7/8 to 22-3/8.
The S&P 500 index fell 2.31 points to 811.34.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.96 points to 1316.76.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
